meta.titulo: Janelas para a Alma | Visual Inclusion and the Fight Against Strabismus
meta.descricao: An Angolan initiative dedicated to visual inclusion, offering interactive therapeutic exercises, support for people with strabismus (amblyopia) and awareness in schools.

AboutSection.oJanelasParaA: Janelas para a Alma is an Angolan startup dedicated to people with strabismus, a condition that affects the alignment of the eyes and can cause double vision, amblyopia or blindness. In Angola, many children, young people and adults live with this condition without proper support, which weighs on their self-esteem, their performance at school and their social integration.
AboutSection.aoMesmoTempoO: At the same time, the environment suffers from the improper disposal of reusable waste. Janelas para a Alma works where these two problems meet, proposing solutions that serve people and the planet at the same time.
AboutSection.segundoORelatorioDa: According to the World Health Organization (WHO) report on global vision published in 2019, at least 2.2 billion people around the world have a vision impairment. Of these, at least 1 billion have a vision impairment that could have been prevented or that has yet to be addressed. Most people with vision impairment are over the age of 50, but the condition affects people of all ages.
AboutSection.lerRelatorioMundialDa: Read the World Report on Vision (WHO) ↗
AboutSection.deAcordoAPesquisa: According to research by the National Library of Medicine through the National Center for Biotechnology Information in 2023, the overall prevalence of strabismus in Africa was estimated at 0.8%. When left untreated, this condition can lead to amblyopia (lazy eye) and permanent loss of binocular vision, significantly affecting the quality of life and educational development of African children.
AboutSection.lerArtigoAcademicoSobre: Read an Academic Article on Strabismus ↗
AboutSection.daInformacaoECaptada: Of information is taken in through vision
AboutSection.estudosCientificosIndicamQue: Scientific studies indicate that approximately 80% of all the information human beings take in from the outside world is processed through vision. This figure underscores how critical eye health is to cognitive development, performance at school and at work, and personal independence. When vision is impaired, the impact reaches every area of life, from learning to social interaction and the ability to work.

AboutTeaserSection.umaEquipaJovemA: A young team transforming vision health in Angola
AboutTeaserSection.somosJovensAngolanosQue: We are young Angolans who decided to face a condition most people prefer to ignore. Every day, we work alongside children, families and partner clinics to detect strabismus and amblyopia early, and to give those who need it most the simple right to see well.
AboutTeaserSection.cadaRastreioFeitoCada: Every screening, every pair of reused glasses and every vision therapy session is a step toward changing not just a gaze, but the whole life around it.
AboutTeaserSection.equipaDoJanelasPara: The Janelas para a Alma team together

CampanhaGamek.noDia12De: On September 12, we held a strabismus awareness campaign on the streets of Gamek, in the city of Luanda.
CampanhaGamek.aComunidadeMeuKamba: At 9:30 a.m., the Meu Kamba Estrábico community, part of Janelas para a Alma, carried out an awareness campaign whose main goal was to share important information about the condition and to present what we offer, the Janelas para a Alma platform. Along the way, we spoke with many people who live with the condition or are close to someone who does.
CampanhaGamek.reafirmamosONossoCompromisso: We reaffirm our commitment to spreading information about strabismus and vision health.

CampanhaGamek.dalvaFilipeExplicaA: Dalva Filipe explains why it matters to bring accurate information to families, counter misdiagnoses and eliminate the stigma surrounding strabismus.
CampanhaGamek.testemunhosInspiradoresDeNoelma: Inspiring accounts from Noelma Silvestre, who has lived with the condition since childhood, and from volunteers Elton Dias and Josefina Afonso on the transformative effect of empathy, information and mutual support on self-esteem.

CuriosidadesSection.oEstrabismoAfectaCerca: Strabismus affects about 4% of the world's population, but many cases are never diagnosed.
CuriosidadesSection.cercaDe80De: About 80% of everything we learn about the world reaches us through vision.
CuriosidadesSection.aAmbliopiaOlhoPreguicoso: Amblyopia ("lazy eye") can only be treated successfully if it is identified early, preferably before age 7.
CuriosidadesSection.oculosUsadosEDevidamente: Used glasses that are properly refurbished can restore clear vision to someone who has never had access to an eye exam.
CuriosidadesSection.osDoisOlhosTrabalham: The two eyes work as a team: small misalignments can be corrected with vision therapy exercises, without surgery.
CuriosidadesSection.emAngolaAMaioria: In Angola, most cases of childhood strabismus are only detected once they are already affecting the child's performance at school.
CuriosidadesSection.piscarOsOlhosRegularmente: Blinking regularly while using screens helps prevent eye strain, since we blink far less when we are focused on a screen.

Faq.simOsDadosDe: Yes. Health data (such as your strabismus screening results) is treated as a special category of data, is collected only with your explicit consent and is protected by appropriate technical security measures. See sections 3 and 9 of our <ligacao>Privacy Policy</ligacao> for more details.
Faq.simAQualquerMomento: Yes, at any time. You can request the deletion of your account and its associated data in Settings or by contacting us directly. This is one of your rights as a data subject. See section 7 (<ligacao>Data Subject Rights</ligacao>) of the Privacy Policy.
Faq.naoORastreioDigital: No. The digital screening and the interactive exercises are preventive and for guidance only: they are not a medical diagnosis and do not replace an in-person eye exam. See the Medical and Legal Notice in section 5 of the <ligacao>Terms of Use</ligacao>.
Faq.soQuandoOUtilizador: Only when you express a direct interest in being referred, and with your explicit consent. We do not sell or share data for third-party commercial purposes. See section 5 (<ligacao>Sharing Data With Third Parties</ligacao>).
Faq.utilizamosApenasCookiesTecnicos: We use only essential technical cookies and, where applicable, analytics cookies to improve your experience, never for third-party advertising. See section 11 (<ligacao>Cookies</ligacao>).

ImpactSection.cuidarDasPessoasE: Caring for people and the planet
ImpactSection.aoTransformarDesafiosEm: By turning challenges into opportunities, Janelas para a Alma builds a bridge between social inclusion and the circular economy.
ImpactSection.inclusaoVisualComOculos: Visual inclusion through affordable glasses and treatment methods, for greater self-esteem and quality of life.
ImpactSection.oJanelasParaA: Janelas para a Alma promotes visual inclusion by distributing affordable glasses and treatment methods adapted to the Angolan context. By restoring the ability to see properly, we restore the self-esteem and quality of life of children, young people and adults living with strabismus. The impact reaches families and communities, breaking the cycle of social exclusion associated with untreated vision conditions.
ImpactSection.reducaoDeResiduosAtraves: Less waste through the reuse of glasses and recyclable materials.
ImpactSection.atravesDaRecolhaE: By collecting and reusing old glasses and recyclable materials, Janelas para a Alma contributes directly to reducing solid waste. Every pair of glasses reused means less trash in landfills and fewer natural resources used to make new ones. This circular economy model turns waste into a tool for social change.
ImpactSection.menorConsumoIndustrialE: Lower industrial consumption and a smaller carbon footprint through sustainable practices.
ImpactSection.aoReduzirANecessidade: By reducing the need to manufacture new glasses and promoting sustainable practices, Janelas para a Alma helps shrink the carbon footprint. Lower industrial consumption means fewer greenhouse gas emissions, less energy used and fewer natural resources extracted. Every local action has a positive effect in the fight against global climate change.
ImpactSection.oficinasECampanhasPara: Workshops and campaigns that prepare aware young people to spread knowledge.
ImpactSection.asOficinasEducativasE: Our educational workshops and awareness campaigns prepare aware young people who go on to spread knowledge in their communities. Through education on vision health and environmental sustainability, we build a network of changemakers who carry the impact of Janelas para a Alma far beyond its direct reach.

Impacto.aNossaPropostaDe: What We Offer: Bringing Together Health, Ecology and Inclusion
Impacto.umaAbordagemIntegradaPara: An integrated approach to transforming vision health in Angola.
Impacto.sistemaQueConectaPacientes: A system that connects patients with vision care partners, making screenings and appointments easier to access through prices adjusted to each user's circumstances.
Impacto.canalDedicadoARecolha: A dedicated channel for collecting and reusing frames. We turn waste into therapeutic materials, lowering costs for patients and reducing environmental impact.
